core.title: Keep Cargo out of the InterlockingRunner
core.given: A source module in the stack's trains tree (profile: trains tree) that defines an InterlockingRunner (not the production TrainRunner module)
core.when: the module is created or changed
core.then: Keep Cargo inside TrainRunner execution: the InterlockingRunner must not reference, mutate, store (artifact_urn -> artifact_data), or route on Cargo.
prefer: The InterlockingRunner reads only the initial action/inputs/state before execution and a completed TrainResult at a declared route boundary.
Leave Cargo to the TrainRunner, which passes it between wagons; wagons read and return artifact objects.
avoid: Cargo references or mutations of a cargo mapping in an InterlockingRunner module.
Storing artifact_urn -> artifact_data runtime values in the interlocking.
Routing on mid-train Cargo state; letting Cargo select train variants.
unless: The production TrainRunner module legitimately constructs and carries Cargo; it is not scanned for Cargo bleed.
core.why: Cargo is the artifact data plane carried by the TrainRunner between wagons inside a selected train; the cargo_boundary keeps it inside that execution, so the interlocking never routes on mid-train Cargo state nor lets Cargo select train variants, routing only on initial inputs and declared-boundary TrainResults.
evidence: The stack's cargo-boundary check reports no Cargo reference, cargo-mapping mutation, or artifact_urn literal in any InterlockingRunner-defining module in the trains tree.

The same check reports no wagon entry module (located via the profile's wagon directory and wagon-module pattern) importing interlocking code — the companion split convention's obligation, enforced by the same realization check.
A reviewer confirms the InterlockingRunner's routing inputs are only the initial action/inputs/state and declared-boundary TrainResults, and that Cargo does not select train variants.
verification: Scan each InterlockingRunner-defining module in the trains tree and flag a Cargo reference, a cargo-mapping mutation, or an artifact_urn literal.

Scan each wagon entry module (located via the profile's wagon directory and wagon-module pattern) and flag an import of interlocking code; that is the companion split convention's obligation, and one realization check may enforce it alongside this one — this core's then covers only the InterlockingRunner Cargo boundary.
Comment text is masked before matching; a string artifact_urn literal is still detected.
The production TrainRunner module is excluded from the Cargo-bleed scan; only InterlockingRunner-defining modules are scanned for Cargo bleed.
Which modules are scanned and how Cargo touches are recognized is the per-stack realization's (detector's) concern.
Severity 4, disposition strict: a newly introduced Cargo touch (or, under the companion convention, a wagon importing interlocking) is not suppressible and fails CI.

values: source module in the trains tree
routing decision depends on mid-train Cargo state

fires: An InterlockingRunner module in the trains tree references Cargo or assigns into a cargo mapping.
An InterlockingRunner caches artifact_urn -> artifact_data values or contains an artifact_urn string literal.
An InterlockingRunner chooses the next route from mid-train Cargo state.
Cargo contents are used to select a train variant.
doesNotFire: The production TrainRunner module constructs Cargo and passes it between wagons.
An InterlockingRunner reads the initial action/inputs/state before execution.
An InterlockingRunner reads a completed TrainResult at a declared route boundary.
A comment inside an InterlockingRunner module mentions Cargo (comments are masked).
A wagon entry module (located via the profile's wagon directory and wagon-module pattern) changes its imports (governed by the companion convention that wagons must not import interlocking code).

neutralityNotes: TrainRunner, InterlockingRunner, Cargo, artifact_urn/artifact_data, TrainResult and wagon are the agnostic ATDD core-runtime spec's own vocabulary (the rule is the realization of the core 'cargo boundary' obligation), so they are kept in the core. The Bun stack, the TypeScript/JavaScript languages (tooling.languages), the src/trains/** trains tree (proposed roles.runtime_components#trains_location), and the src/<wagon>/wagon.ts wagon-module location (layout.wagon_dir plus proposed layout.locations#wagon_module) all come from the profile; the `cargo[...] = ...` token form is generalized to 'cargo-mapping mutation' (the concrete form stays in bun.json as the reference example), and only the detector family/check-file ids and the companion split-convention rule id remain in bunOnly. The wagon-must-not-import-interlocking half is the companion split convention's obligation; the core keeps it only as a generic, profile-parameterized note in evidence/verification so no extra obligation is added.
